text:
maria (CSE): Heads up — CinderPay reported sustained 429s from their Dedicated pool during a marketing blast at ~15:04 UTC. They see TPS drop and admission controller denying requests due to burst credit exhaustion.

maria (CSE): Sample error from customer:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req-9a2bf3
x-pool-id: ded-pool-42
error: admission_rejected_burst_credits
```

maria (CSE): Pool: ded-pool-42 in us-west-2. Customer claims they had reserved capacity, not shared. They've attached a 1-minute trace with a ~6k tokens/s spike.

jake (oncall): Looking. Any quick repro steps from CinderPay? Did they change model size or burst config?

maria (CSE): They say no model swap — same t5-large v2. Their client did start fanout (x10) for campaign. Repro curl from their side:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cinder" \
  -d '{"model":"t5-large-v2","prompt":"...","max_tokens":256}'
```

leo (infra): I see ded-pool-42 admission logs. Burst credits dropped to zero at 15:03:52. Autoscaler did not spin up more nodes because pool hit quota check; there was an admission controller gating due to headroom_policy=conservative.

leo (infra): Also noticed GPU memory errors on node gpu-12 at 15:02:40 — several OOMs from a different tenant causing eviction and reduced available slots. Noisy neighbor suspected.

sophia (billing): Quick check — CinderPay has reserved capacity but their burst credit refill schedule is hourly. Their account had an outstanding billing auth event but it was resolved at 15:05 — refill didn't backfill past spike.

maria (CSE): So multiple factors: (1) sudden client fanout causing token/s spike, (2) noisy neighbor OOMs reducing effective pool capacity, (3) burst credit accounting/refill timing + conservative headroom policy.

hugo (customer): Thanks everyone. Is there a recommended mitigation so campaign can resume? We saw ~15% failed requests overall.

jake (oncall): Short term: increase headroom manually for ded-pool-42 and temporarily loosen admission headroom_policy to permissive. Also ask CinderPay to reduce client fanout to x3 while we stabilize.

leo (infra): I'll add a node to the pool (prewarm) and drain gpu-12. Also toggling admission headroom to permissive now.

ops-bot: action=update_headroom pool=ded-pool-42 policy=permissive user=jake ts=1765303100

leo (infra): Added node gpu-21 to pool, prewarm in progress (ETA 90s).

sophia (billing): For long term: we should revisit burst credit refill logic to allow emergency backfill on resolved billing events inside a short window (5m grace). I'll open a ticket to product.

maria (CSE): Repro plan for eng-runtime:
- Simulate fanout x10 with same model and request shape (256 tokens) ramping to 6k tokens/s for 60s
- Inject a noisy-tenant job that triggers GPU OOMs on one node
- Observe admission controller: burst decrement, admission deny rate, autoscaler decisions

maria (CSE): Commands to reproduce locally (dev cluster):
```
# ramp tool (wrk-like)
./ramp --qps 500 --concurrency 10 --clients 10 --payload ./sample.json --duration 60 --header "Authorization: Bearer sk-test"

# noisy worker (simulate memory pressure)
python stress_gpu.py --alloc-gb 20 --duration 70
```

jake (oncall): Good. Eng-runtime, can you validate admission controller prioritization behavior? Specifically: when burst credits==0 and headroom_policy=conservative, autoscaler should override and add nodes if utilization > 85% for 30s. Current logs show we skipped scaling because billing_quota_check=false.

leo (infra): Noted — looks like billing_quota_check blocked autoscale until refill confirmed. I'll add a temporary override to allow autoscale when queue backlog > 500 requests.

ops-bot: action=add_node_override pool=ded-pool-42 override_reason="emergency-autoscale" user=leo ts=1765303345

maria (CSE): Customer update: they reduced fanout to x3; errors dropped to ~2% after headroom change and node add. They want a postmortem and a plan to avoid future campaign interruptions.

sophia (billing): I'll coordinate with product on two items: burst credit refill grace window and a billing/authorization signal to autoscaler that shouldn't block emergency scaling briefly.

jake (oncall): Next steps for eng-runtime + infra:
- Repro on staging using maria's steps
- Adjust admission controller rules: allow emergency autoscale override when backlog > threshold even if burst credits=0
- Consider preferential throttling for noisy tenants (identify by slot usage)
- Create runbook: notify CSE and optionally prewarm dedicated pools before large known campaigns

maria (CSE): I'll draft the customer communication and recommend prewarm + lower fanout. Also request a dedicated pre-campaign capacity check with solutions eng for high-risk customers.

hugo (customer): Appreciate the quick fixes. Please share the runbook and timing for permanent fixes.

maria (CSE): Will share once eng confirms repro and proposed admission changes. Leaving thread open until we have staging repro + PR.

leo (infra): Recording follow-ups: infra-#1129 (autoscale-override), runtime-#845 (admission-emergency-scaling), billing-#297 (burst-refill-grace). Assigning owners.

jake (oncall): Closing immediate incident — monitor for 15m. If errors creep back, reopen and escalate to eng-runtime.

ops-bot: monitor=ded-pool-42 metric=admission_denies window=15m threshold=1% alert_channel=#incidents ts=1765303921

maria (CSE): Thanks all. Customer satisfied for now, will await the runbook and PRs.
